ideia: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus, meaning it takes longer to rotate once on its axis than to complete an orbit around the Sun.
There is a giant gas cloud in the center of our galaxy that contains enough ethyl alcohol to fill 400 trillion trillion pints of beer.
Neutron stars are so incredibly dense that a single teaspoon of their material would weigh about 6 billion tons on Earth.
Deep in the atmospheres of Neptune and Uranus, the intense pressure is so high that it literally rains diamonds.
According to astronauts, open space smells like a distinct mixture of hot metal, diesel fumes, and seared steak.
Wombats are the only known animals in the world that produce cube-shaped feces, which prevents the droppings from rolling away.
Flamingos are not born pink; they are actually grey, and their feathers turn pink due to a natural dye in their diet of shrimp and algae.
A grizzly bear's bite is strong enough to crush a bowling ball, exerting a pressure of over 1,100 pounds per square inch.
Sea otters hold hands with each other while they sleep so they don't drift apart in the ocean currents.
Cows have best friends within their herds and become visibly stressed and anxious when they are separated from them.
Male Gentoo penguins search the entire beach to find the smoothest, most perfect pebble to present as a marriage proposal to their mate.
Human teeth are the only part of the body that cannot heal or repair themselves because they are not made of living tissue.
The human nose can remember and distinguish between more than 50,000 different unique scents.
The human body actually glows in the dark, emitting a tiny amount of bioluminescent light that is 1,000 times weaker than our eyes can detect.
Signals and information travel along your nerves and throughout your brain at speeds of up to 268 miles per hour.
Your brain uses about 20% of your body's total energy and oxygen, despite making up only 2% of your body's total weight.
The water pressure at the deepest point of the ocean is equivalent to having an elephant standing directly on your thumb.
There are more historic artifacts and shipwrecks lying at the bottom of the ocean than in all of the world's museums combined.
Jellyfish are made of 95% water and survive perfectly fine without a brain, a heart, bones, or a central nervous system.
The loudest sound ever recorded in the ocean was a mysterious low-frequency noise called 'The Bloop', which was later identified as a massive icequake.
Despite modern technology, more than 80% of the Earth's vast oceans remain completely unexplored, unmapped, and unseen by humans.
The oldest known written customer complaint is a 3,800-year-old clay tablet from ancient Mesopotamia complaining about a delivery of sub-standard copper.
In ancient Egypt, Pharaohs would order their servants to be covered in honey to attract pesky flies away from the rulers.
In ancient Rome, the sweat of popular gladiators was collected and sold in small vials to wealthy women to use as a facial cosmetic.
Before modern alarm clocks existed, people called 'knocker-ups' were paid to shoot dried peas at workers' windows to wake them up for work.
In 1325, two rival Italian city-states started a military conflict known as the 'War of the Bucket' after soldiers stole an oak bucket from a well.
Under the right conditions of temperature and pressure, water can boil and freeze at the exact same time, a phenomenon known as the 'triple point'.
When cooled to near absolute zero, liquid helium becomes a superfluid, allowing it to flow upward against gravity and climb out of containers.
Bananas contain high levels of potassium-40, which makes them very slightly radioactive, though you'd have to eat millions at once to be harmed.
Lightning strikes the Earth's surface approximately 100 times every single second, releasing immense energy.
Sound waves travel about four times faster through water than they do through the air because water molecules are packed tighter.
The very first computer mouse was invented in 1964 and was constructed almost entirely out of a carved block of wood.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was intentionally designed to slow down typists so that mechanical arms on early typewriters wouldn't jam.
The first computer 'bug' was a literal insect—a moth that got stuck inside a Harvard Mark II computer relay in 1947.
The total weight of all the active man-made satellites orbiting Earth is actually less than the weight of a single modern cruise ship.
There is a small, cold town in Norway named Hell, and its local river and streets regularly freeze over completely during the winter.
Canada has more natural lakes than the rest of the world's countries combined, containing about 60% of all the lakes on Earth.
The Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest place on Earth, with some weather stations there having never recorded a single drop of rain.
Pure honey never spoils; archaeologists have discovered 3,000-year-old pots of honey in Egyptian tombs that are still perfectly edible.
Cashews grow on the bottom of a strange, yellow-orange fruit called the cashew apple, and their raw outer shells are highly toxic.
